scope: Shared backing for finite Split and extracted component index buffers when cross-origin isolation and SharedArrayBuffer are available; the ordinary-buffer fallback remains unchanged.
behavior: Both merge-sort buffers are shared because either can become the finished Split index array. Component compaction fills a shared index array before publication. Existing worker transport retains shared buffers without putting them in the transfer list; geometry, order and MCP contracts are unchanged.

validation.focused: 166 tests passed across Split seams, component operations, processing workers, project reuse and publication; both sort-buffer parities, isolated and non-isolated behavior, shared-buffer unavailability and binary chunk reuse are covered.
validation.build: Production build scanforge-678d8b5f043b099b and all 14 TypeScript batches passed; recorded peak 1465659392 bytes. An earlier build failed because the new test did not narrow the array-or-typed-array index type; it was corrected and the build rerun.
validation.workerSplit: An isolated production-build browser observed four shared 21-index Split outputs across the worker boundary. The finite-interior GUI and public MCP results matched, with history, binary reopen, held-result MCP cancellation and GUI close cancellation checks passing; recorded peak 964898816 bytes.
validation.originalPly1: On the 274154-face original scan, GUI and public MCP Extract geometry matched; both worker results had shared 422451-index buffers. Source and cutter remained unchanged and GUI Undo passed. A separate run downloaded and reopened a 32518213-byte project through the GUI with matching source, cutter and extracted geometry; Undo/Redo was exercised before reopening. Recorded peaks were 1318182912 and 1412091904 bytes.
validation.combinedPreview: The running 5173 preview passed the same PLY-1 GUI/public-MCP Extract comparison, and both worker outputs had shared 422451-index buffers; recorded peak 1383538688 bytes. A separate combined-preview finite-interior lifecycle probe timed out waiting for a held GUI worker result during cancellation; it cleaned up and is not counted as a pass. The isolated production build passed that cancellation scenario.
validation.originalPly2: On the 2697877-face original scan, GUI Split/Extract, pre-reopen Undo/Redo, a 350247269-byte public-MCP artifact download and GUI reopen completed with matching source, cutter and extracted core geometry. The recorded peak was 3276959744 bytes; cleanup confirmed. The downloaded SHA-256 08e732bb2dacd2a8f695b2fce38236174208dc525875855d5b2814ce06648d81 was not independently compared to the exported artifact.

acceptanceGuard: A task-local copy of the existing 4 GiB Windows Job guard now rejects missing or above-limit reported peak values. Its policy tests and a small real Job passed, and it correctly rejected the previously reported 4300234752-byte peak that the older guard called a pass. The job limit applies to committed memory; the peak counter is a separate measurement, so the strict peak criterion is conservative and does not establish why a peak exceeded the nominal limit. The original guard and other tasks were not modified.
review: Independent review found no concrete ownership defect. Both buffers remain private while being filled, and the processing worker excludes SharedArrayBuffer from transfers; browser and codec checks address the noted worker-boundary gap.
limitations: The 3691133-face PLY-3 full-download GUI reopen remains unresolved, as do native Split and the remaining M2 acceptance criteria.
The PLY-2 run did not test public-MCP Extract, post-reopen Undo/Redo, independent artifact hash equality, native output or general memory bounds.
The combined preview cancellation timeout has not been diagnosed and is not evidence that cancellation passed there.
The isolated Float64 decoder-view and restore-race prototypes remain unmerged; their focused tests do not establish end-to-end safety.
